newsitem.title: INDIA: Red tape tangles British firms in India - envoy.
newsitem.headline: Red tape tangles British firms in India - envoy.

text.p: British companies want to invest in India but are hampered by red tape, Britain's embassy in New Delhi said on Wednesday.

"Many British companies in sectors such as power, telecommunications and insurance are eager to invest in India, but are being prevented by bureaucratic delays," High Commissioner Sir David Gore-Booth said in a statement.

He was responding to local newspaper reports about a poor response by British companies to an Indo-British trade fair planned in October in New Delhi to mark India's 50th anniversary of independence from Britain.

"Reports in some newspapers here that the take-up has been poor are rubbish. In fact the response has been exceptional. Indeed there is now a waiting list of companies queueing up to participate," Gore-Booth said.
The embassy said 130 companies have signed up to exhibit at the fair and that a target for two-way trade of five billion pounds ($8.1 billion) by the year 2000 has been set.
Last year, two-way trade stood at 3.2 billion pounds, it added. ($ = 0.615 British Pounds)
